articles.title: Torcedor cai de arquibancada superior do Couto Pereira em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens gravadas por outro torcedor mostram a queda, na noite de sexta-feira (11). Homem ficou ferido e foi levado ao Hospital do Trabalhador.
articles.summary: Imagens gravadas por outro torcedor mostram a queda, na noite de sexta-feira (11). Homem ficou ferido e foi levado ao Hospital do Trabalhador.
articles.body:
Um homem de 49 anos caiu da arquibancada superior do Estádio Couto Pereira, em Curitiba , na noite de sexta-feira (12). A queda foi filmada por outro torcedor e o vídeo viralizou nas redes sociais. Assista acima.

O torcedor recebeu atendimento ainda no estádio e foi levado de ambulância para o Hospital do Trabalhador, em Curitiba. Não há informações sobre como ele caiu nem sobre o estado de saúde dele. A Polícia Civil investiga o caso.

A situação aconteceu durante o clássico entre Coritiba e Athletico Paranaense.

O vídeo mostra primeiro um momento da partida. Em seguida, algo cai da arquibancada superior, aparentando ser uma peça de roupa. Segundos depois, um homem de calça jeans e sem camisa despenca. Torcedores se assustam e questionam o que aconteceu.

O clube informou que acompanha o caso e presta o suporte necessário, mas afirmou que não pode informar o estado de saúde do torcedor.

O g1 entrou em contato com a assessoria de imprensa do hospital para verificar o estado de saúde do homem, mas não recebeu retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

Em nota, a Polícia Civil (PC-PR) afirmou que investiga o caso.

Torcedor cai de arquibancada superior do Couto Pereira durante jogo em Curitiba — Foto: Redes sociais

13º no estado desde o começo do ano: Novo tornado é registrado no Paraná

O jogo clássico entre Coritiba e Athletico Paranaense foi válido pela 27ª rodada do Brasileirão, e terminou empatado. O Athletico chegou a abrir 3x1 contra o Coritiba, mas o Coxa conseguiu o empate com 3x3 em casa.

Os gols foram marcados por Tiago Cóser, e Rodrigo Moledo (dois gols) do Coritiba, e por Luiz Gustavo, Arthur Dias, e Viveros do Athletico Paranaense.

articles.title: Mulher conta como descobriu que foi infectada com HIV pelo namorado | G1
articles.standfirst: Jean José Dunga foi condenado a pagar indenização de R$ 50 mil. Vítima procurou médica e descobriu que o Ministério Público já investigava seu namorado por outros casos semelhantes no estado.
articles.summary: Jean José Dunga foi condenado a pagar indenização de R$ 50 mil. Vítima procurou médica e descobriu que o Ministério Público já investigava seu namorado por outros casos semelhantes
articles.body:
"Fui contaminada de forma intencional": A frase marcou o momento em que Marta* entendeu que a infecção por HIV não havia sido um acaso, mas resultado da conduta do então namorado , o dentista Jean José Dunga, de 41 anos, em Porto Velho .

Em uma entrevista para o g1 , a vítima contou que soube que o namorado tinha HIV por meio de terceiros, e não pelo próprio suspeito. No dia 19 de maio de 2026, o exame sorológico dela deu positivo para HIV. Uma semana depois, no dia 26 de maio, exames complementares confirmaram a infecção.

Antes disso, ela enfrentava uma sequência de sintomas que não melhoravam. Ela relata ter sofrido com infecções recorrentes, dores no corpo, vermelhidão, coceira, dor de cabeça e cansaço.

Segundo Marta, os problemas de saúde começaram em menos de um mês após o início do relacionamento. Como os sintomas persistiam mesmo após o uso de medicamentos, ela decidiu fazer exames para investigar a causa do quadro. Com a piora do estado de saúde, descobriu que estava infectada pelo HIV.

"Terminei com o Jean no dia 30 de abril e depois dessa data nunca mais voltamos a nos falar. Ele nunca me falou que tinha HIV quando namorávamos", relata.

🔎O HIV é o Vírus da Imunodeficiência Humana. Ele invade e enfraquece o sistema imunológico, que protege o corpo contra doenças. Caso não haja tratamento, ele pode causar a Aids (termo para Síndrome da Imunodeficiência Adquirida, em inglês).

*Para proteger a identidade da vítima, que teme o estigma social e a exposição de sua família, ela é identificada nesta reportagem pelo nome fictício de Marta. A identidade do acusado é real.

Jean José Dunga de Oliveira — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Vítima

A confirmação foi acompanhada de outra revelação: durante consulta com uma médica infectologista, a paciente foi informada de que o Ministério Público de Rondônia (MP-RO) já monitorava um dentista suspeito de infectar mulheres intencionalmente no estado.

A vítima contou que só descobriu a ligação entre o namorado e a investigação quando informou o nome dele durante o atendimento médico.

"A médica me deu essa notícia com muito respeito cuidado e muita ponderação, pois estava num estado emocional muito delicado. Já havia preparado minha família para que eu pudesse ter forças para entender que fui contaminada de forma intencional, ou seja, de forma criminosa, por uma pessoa que havia usufruído de toda intimidade da minha casa e família", relembra.

Segundo Marta, a informação transformou o choque do diagnóstico em indignação. Ela afirma que, naquele momento, descobriu que não era a primeira mulher a denunciar o dentista.

A médica orientou a vítima a procurar o Núcleo de Atendimento a Vítimas (Navit) do Ministério Público. Lá, ela descobriu que era a quarta mulher a denunciá-lo. Jean foi preso em junho de 2026 e permanece detido em Porto Velho.

"Quando fui infectada pelo Jean, ele não adoeceu somente a mim, ele adoeceu uma família inteira. Há um luto, ele atingiu todas as pessoas que me amam e estão ao meu lado", afirmou a vítima ao g1.

Segundo o MP-RO, a primeira denúncia foi feita no dia 4 de dezembro de 2025. A mulher relatou que sofreu violência sexual e depois descobriu estar contaminada com HIV. A segunda vítima foi ouvida seis dias depois, relatando o mesmo crime.

Em janeiro de 2026, a terceira pessoa foi encaminhada ao Navit por meio do Serviço de Atendimento Especializado (SAE), uma unidade localizada em Porto Velho que oferece testagem e tratamento para pessoas que vivem com HIV e Aids.

Os casos das três primeiras vítimas resultaram em um processo único. Jean foi denunciado à Justiça por lesão corporal gravíssima e perigo de contágio de doença grave. Em relação a duas das mulheres, ele também foi acusado de estupro.

De acordo com o MP-RO, a investigação sobre Jean já estava em andamento havia cerca de quatro meses quando Marta recebeu o diagnóstico.

No caso de Marta, Jean foi condenado a cinco anos de prisão em regime semiaberto e ao pagamento de R$ 50 mil em indenização à vítima.

Antes da condenação, a defesa de Jean prestou solidariedade às vítimas e afirmou ao g1 que o acusado realizava tratamento antirretroviral e acreditava não haver risco de transmissão sexual do HIV. Após a condenação, a reportagem voltou a procurar o advogado, que optou por não se pronunciar.

Ao denunciar o caso, Marta procurou o Navit em busca de acolhimento e apoio. Segundo ela, a decisão de procurar as autoridades também foi motivada pelo receio de que outras mulheres pudessem ser vítimas do mesmo homem.

Homem é condenado por transmitir HIV de propósito em RO — Foto: arte/g1

De acordo com o MP-RO, é possível que existam outras vítimas ainda não identificadas. Caso haja a confirmação do diagnóstico, as vítimas em Rondônia podem procurar o Navit:

Qualquer pessoa que desconfie ter sido exposta ao vírus pode procurar as Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS) ou as UPAs para realizar o teste rápido de forma gratuita e sigilosa. O município de Porto Velho também conta com o atendimento do SAE.

articles.title: Servidor é afastado por bater ponto no ES enquanto faz Medicina no RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Denúncia do Ministério Público do Espírito Santo diz que farmacêutico recebe salário sem cumprir devidamente a carga horária.
articles.summary: O servidor de Afonso Cláudio foi afastado após denúncia do MPES apontar que ele recebia salário sem trabalhar para cursar Medicina em outro estado.
articles.body:
A Justiça do Espírito Santo determinou o afastamento cautelar de um servidor público de Afonso Cláudio , na Região Serrana do estado, suspeito de seguir recebendo salário sem cumprir devidamente a carga horária no cargo de farmacêutico na cidade.

Segundo denúncia do Ministério Público Estadual (MPES), Gustavo Henrique de Freitas Silva batia ponto como se estivesse no local de trabalho, enquanto, na verdade, estava fazendo as aulas do curso de Medicina, de forma presencial, em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana, no Rio de Janeiro. A distância entre as duas cidades é de mais de 150 km.

Ainda de acordo com o órgão ministerial, dados relacionados a antenas de celular apontaram que o servidor estava a cerca de 200 quilômetros de Afonso Cláudio, quando sua frequência era registrada nos plantões da Secretaria de Saúde da cidade da Região Serrana do Espírito Santo.

Nesta quinta-feira (10), a prefeitura informou ter oficializado o afastamento do servidor .

Já Gustavo Henrique reforçou o caráter provisório da medida e disse que esta será devidamente questionada por sua defesa. Ele faz Medicina desde 2023 no estado vizinho.

Ele acrescentou ainda que "as alegações apresentadas pelo Ministério Público não refletem integralmente a realidade dos fatos".

De acordo com a denúncia do MPES, Gustavo Henrique, que é servidor concursado da prefeitura desde 2017, foi escalado para cumprir plantões de 48 horas aos finais de semana na Agência Transfusional do Hospital São Vicente de Paulo.

A escala, entretanto, não estaria sendo efetivamente cumprida.

“A permanência do servidor na escala de plantões, quando há provas de que fisicamente se encontra em outra unidade da federação, não apenas facilita a ocultação do ilícito, como expõe a grave risco o funcionamento da Agência Transfusional local. A medida cautelar é imperiosa para estancar a lesão”, afirma o juiz Jorge Orrevan Vaccari Filho, em decisão assinada em 4 de agosto.

A representação do MPES se baseou em análise técnica realizada com autorização da Justiça, em que ficou demonstrado que nos plantões de finais de semana escalados para os meses de setembro e outubro de 2024, o servidor aparecia com frequência registrada, apesar de estar fisicamente no Rio de Janeiro.

Para o órgão ministerial, esse fato comprovou a falsidade das informações registradas em sua ficha funcional.

Apesar do asfaltamento cautelar, a decisão mantém o direito de o servidor seguir recebendo seus vencimentos no período em que estiver fora do cargo. Ele, contudo, não poderá receber verbas indenizatórias ou compensações por eventuais horas extras.

Por fim, a decisão determina que a Prefeitura de Afonso Cláudio adote medidas administrativas e disciplinares sobre o caso, além de controle rigoroso da frequência de servidores.

Câmara Municipal de Afonso Cláudio, no Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/PMAC

No último dia 28, o Ministério Público encaminhou um ofício à Câmara de Vereadores de Afonso Cláudio, informando ao Legislativo sobre a ação judicial envolvendo o servidor da prefeitura, para eventuais providências da Casa de Leis, em função de seu dever fiscalizatório.

Em conversa com o g1 na tarde desta quinta-feira (10), o presidente da Câmara, vereador Marcelo Costa (PSB), confirmou que recebeu o documento do MPES na última sexta (4).

"O ofício foi lido na sessão de hoje (quinta). Agora, o próximo passo será pedir informações da prefeitura, para analisarmos que providências tomaremos", disse o chefe do Legislativo.

Prefeitura diz ter aberto processo disciplinar

A reportagem do g1 também conversou sobre a decisão com o prefeito Luciano Pimenta (PP), na tarde desta quinta (10). Segundo o mandatário, o servidor já teria sido afastado e um Procedimento Administrativo Disciplinar (PAD) teria sido aberto para apurar as ausências nos plantões.

Pimenta também compartilhou nota pública em que a prefeitura afirma ter sido notificada da decisão. No comunicado o Executivo informa ainda que "já adotou as medidas administrativas e legais cabíveis para o seu integral cumprimento".

“A administração municipal esclarece que os fatos estão sendo analisados pelos setores competentes, com a verificação dos registros funcionais, do efetivo cumprimento da jornada de trabalho, dos pagamentos realizados e das demais circunstâncias relacionadas ao caso”, informa a nota da prefeitura.

Por fim, a prefeitura conclui a nota afirmando que, "caso sejam constatadas irregularidades, serão adotadas todas as providências previstas em lei, inclusive para a apuração e individualização de eventuais responsabilidades".

articles.title: Médico mapeia a vida selvagem no próprio bairro e mobiliza vizinhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Há cinco anos promovendo exposições na praça do San Conrado, o anestesista Ricardo Lima já catalogou mais de 200 espécies de aves e hoje monitora felino ameaçado de extinção na região.
articles.summary: Há cinco anos promovendo exposições na praça do San Conrado, o anestesista Ricardo Lima já catalogou mais de 200 espécies de aves e hoje monitora felino ameaçado de extinção.
articles.body:
Em 2019, o Terra da Gente contou a história do médico anestesista Ricardo Lima, morador de Campinas (SP), que mostrava como transformou o quintal de casa em um refúgio para a vida silvestre , registrando cerca de 100 espécies de aves e animais como tatus e pacas.

Anos depois, a história ganhou um novo patamar: o catálogo do San Conrado e entorno saltou para mais de 210 espécies de aves, e o monitoramento do médico revelou a presença de um morador nobre e ilustre, o gato-do-mato-pequeno , felino ameaçado de extinção que consta na Lista Vermelha da IUCN.

Flagrado duas vezes através de câmeras trap instaladas por Ricardo, o pequeno predador virou a grande estrela da fauna local e o símbolo de um trabalho que vai além do encanto visual.

“A gente não pode cuidar daquilo que não conhece”, pontua o médico, ressaltando o papel da fotografia no engajamento dos vizinhos com a biodiversidade que divide espaço com o bairro.

Entre os registros de aves, a presença do tiê-sangue também marcou a trajetória do observador no local.

“Apareceu na época mais aguda da pandemia. Além de ser raro por aqui, é um grande representante da nossa Mata Atlântica”.

Veja mais notícias do Terra da Gente, no g1:

Exposição comunitária transforma praça em galeria a céu aberto

Para transformar a contemplação em ação prática, Ricardo promove neste dia 20, das 8h30 às 16h30, a 5ª Exposição de Fotografia na Praça do San Conrado . O evento aposta na simplicidade e na participação comunitária: os moradores e convidados levam seus próprios registros impressos em folha A4 e fixam o material em um varal com dois pregadores de madeira.

“O objetivo foi divulgar a fotografia, o birdwatching, a aproximação entre os moradores e o despertar com a natureza e a fauna”, explica o idealizador. Por ser realizada ao ar livre e em um espaço amplo, a organização não limitou a quantidade de fotos expostas.

Mais do que um encontro cultural, a exposição é um chamado à responsabilidade coletiva diante dos perigos que a fauna silvestre enfrenta no ambiente urbano.

“Temos que trabalhar muito em relação aos animais domésticos, principalmente gatos, que afetam diretamente o equilíbrio da natureza. Temos que trazer a população para esse lado”, alerta o médico.

A urgência desse debate ficou ainda mais evidente após um episódio recente com os macacos-bugio do bairro. Dizimados no estado de São Paulo durante a epidemia de febre amarela, a espécie voltou a dar ar da graça no ano passado, para a surpresa de Ricardo. No entanto, a convivência com a estrutura urbana trouxe tragédias recentes:

“Há poucas semanas, tivemos um acidente grave. Um bugio se perdeu, entrou no condomínio e foi eletrocutado. Levaram de imediato para a clínica veterinária, mas o quadro era grave. Estou tentando na prefeitura uma passagem de fauna e acho que podemos fazer um trabalho melhor”.

Entre a rotina médica e o monitoramento diário na mata, Ricardo segue acompanhando os passos do gato-do-mato-pequeno e da fauna local.

“Esse é um animal que eu tenho acompanhado bastante, e vamos ver por quanto tempo ele vai nos dar o prazer da companhia”, conclui.

articles.title: Jovem morto e outro ferido a tiros em Piraí; polícia investiga | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu na Estrada do Andrade, na Serra do Matoso.
articles.summary: Jovem morto em Piraí e outro ferido foram localizados na Serra do Matoso; a falta de sinal de telefone dificultou o resgate da vítima sobrevivente após o crime.
articles.body:
Um jovem, de 19 anos, foi encontrado morto e outro, de 18, foi baleado em Piraí (RJ). O caso aconteceu na Estrada do Andrade, na Serra do Matoso na noite de quinta-feira (10) mas, só foi divulgado neste sábado (12).

Os agentes foram acionados, na sexta-feira (11), para verificar a denúncia de uma possível pessoa ferida por disparo de arma de fogo. Segundo a Polícia Militar , no local, testemunhas indicaram uma residência, onde um jovem ferido estava desde a noite anterior.

Ainda de acordo com a corporação, a mãe da vítima disse aos agentes que devido às chuvas, não havia sinal de internet ou telefone funcionando para que pudessem pedir socorro.

Em seguida, ele foi socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e encaminhado para o Hospital Flávio Leal.

A Polícia Militar informou que testemunhas também indicaram o local onde uma outra vítima estava. Ele foi encontrado já sem vida pelos agentes.

Uma equipe de perícia esteve no local para levantar informações que possam ajudar nas investigações. Em seguida, o corpo foi removido para o Instituto Médico Legal (IML) .

O caso foi registrado na delegacia de Piraí, que está responsável pelas investigações. Até o momento da publicação desta reportagem, ninguém havia sido preso, as motivações do caso e a causa da morte eram desconhecidas.

A identidade dos envolvidos não foi divulgada.

articles.title: Three minutes of all-out exercise may trigger more health-related changes in the blood than 90 minutes of moderate cycling: New study explains why

articles.body: When we talk about exercise, most people think a good workout has to be long: a sweat session that chews up an hour or more. But what if a workout that lasts only a few minutes could send a stronger molecular signal through the body than an hour and a half of steady exercise? New research suggests something wild: just three minutes of truly all-out effort can set off a bigger wave of change in your blood than a workout thirty times longer.That’s what scientists discovered when they looked at short, intense bursts of exercise, specifically, three minutes of maximum-effort cycling, chopped up as six 30-second sprints with four-minute breaks between. After those sprints, researchers found dramatic shifts in hundreds of proteins and tiny molecules in the blood. In fact, the changes were leaps and bounds bigger than what they saw when people cycled moderately for a full 90 minutes. Suddenly, it looked like intensity (not just duration) plays a massive role in how exercise tells your body to adapt, upgrade, or maybe even heal.And here’s the kicker: nobody’s saying that three minutes of sprinting will replace a longer workout, or that these short efforts guarantee you’ll dodge heart disease or diabetes. What the science shows is that the blood’s molecular response to maximal effort is immediate and intense, but not necessarily a stand-in for every benefit of staying active.What did the new exercise study find?The research, published in Cell Reports Medicine and led out of Rockefeller University, set up two groups. One group pushed through six half-minute cycling sprints, with rest in between, so only three minutes of real effort but more time in total for recovery. The other group just cycled steadily for an hour and a half. Blood samples were taken before the workout, right after, and again three hours later.The difference was clear. After sprinting, nearly a quarter of the blood’s 2,800-some proteins had changed. With moderate cycling, that number was less than a quarter of a percent. Sprinting also switched up more than 200 metabolites, as those tiny molecules are involved in essential chemistry.So, why does intense exercise cause such a dramatic response?The scientists think it’s about how tissues talk to each other under stress. A bunch of the proteins triggered by sprints are linked to building new blood vessels, tweaking hormones, and helping different organs communicate. Many of these proteins also tie into heart and metabolic health.To go even further, the researchers looked at a huge database from the UK Biobank and found that of 33 proteins known to lower metabolic disease risk, 32 were changed by sprinting, while only 3 budged after moderate cycling. Some of these proteins are also connected to biological aging. That’s a strong sign that it’s not just about how long you exercise, but how hard you push yourself, even for short bursts.Does this mean three minutes of sprinting is better than a 90-minute workout?Before you trade your entire workout routine for three minutes of pain, hold on. The study only looked at the blood’s reaction right after exercising; it didn’t measure weight loss, long-term heart health, or how well people aged. Plus, the people involved were young, healthy, and already somewhat active. If you’re older, out of shape, or have medical issues, these results might not apply in the same way. And while sprints supercharged molecular change, most of those proteins went back to normal a few hours later. We don’t know yet if making those changes over and over leads to better health long term.So, should you start sprinting for three minutes?Well, the research adds weight to the idea that short, intense bursts of exercise are more than just time-savers; they really fire up the body in ways we’re only beginning to understand. Prior studies show that very brief sprint sessions can boost fitness, lower blood pressure, and help metabolic health, even when people only do a handful of intense minutes each week.But let’s be clear: “all-out” isn’t a casual jog. It’s exhausting, and not everyone’s built for it — certainly not without working up slowly or talking to a doctor, especially if you’ve been sedentary or have heart concerns.The bigger takeaway isn’t that you have to abandon your usual workout. It’s that exercise doesn’t have to eat up hours to matter. A mere three-minute blast (when it’s done safely and appropriately) might be enough to trigger sweeping changes in your body, and that’s great news for anyone struggling to find time to fit in a workout. At the same time, don’t write off the classic longer sessions, as those still have well-proven, long-term benefits. The real win is realizing that both short and long approaches have a place, and even mini bursts of effort can be worth making time for.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Cyclospora: largest US outbreak of explosive diarrhoea parasite is over, health officials say
articles.summary: More than 12,000 cases of cyclosporiasis, including two deaths, were linked to imported lettuce.
articles.body:
The largest outbreak of an intestinal infection that spread across several US states and affected more than 12,000 people has ended, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) announced on Friday.

Two people have died and 570 were hospitalised in recent months in relation to the outbreak of cyclospora, a microscopic parasite that can cause explosive diarrhoea.

In an advisory notice saying the outbreak was over, the CDC said cases had "significantly declined", and it was continuing to investigate the cause of the infection.

Officials have linked the outbreak, which affected 21 states, to lettuce imported from Mexico by Taylor Farms, a key supplier for many US food outlets.

Taylor Farms announced a voluntary recall of lettuce sourced from central Mexico, while the US fast-food chain Taco Bell said it has removed lettuce from the supplier from its menu.

Cyclospora causes an intestinal illness called cyclosporiasis. It is spread through contaminated food or water and can cause symptoms including severe diarrhoea.

The CDC says deaths from cyclosporiasis are uncommon, as it is "not usually life-threatening".

Health officials in Michigan said that the two deaths, which both happened in the state, were of people who had "significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration".

According to CDC data, there have been nearly 20,000 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases since 1 May, as well as more than 1,000 hospitalisations. Forty-nine states, as well as DC, have reported cases.

The agency notes that the true number of people who have been sick with the parasite is likely to be much higher.

While the majority of these were linked to the contaminated lettuce, thousands were not.

UK health officials too have warned about the outbreak following recent cases contracted by returning travellers.

Before the latest outbreak the worst year for infections was 2019, when there were about 4,700 across the country.

articles.title: ACA, Medicare or health insurance through work? Your health insurance bills are about to go up
articles.summary: Most Americans can expect to pay significantly more each month for health insurance next year, whether they get it through work, Obamacare or Medicare.
articles.body: Most Americans can expect to pay significantly more each month for health insurance next year, whether they get it through work, Obamacare or Medicare. In some cases, the premium increases may be the largest in decades and are driven by numerous economic pressures. But they won’t look the same for everyone. Some will pay more in the form of higher copays or deductibles. “Healthcare costs are going up faster than they have in years, and open enrollment is when the healthcare affordability crisis is really going to hit home for people,” said Larry Levitt, executive vice president for health policy at KFF, a nonpartisan research group. “That’s true for whatever kind of insurance you have.” Prices have shifted upward in every corner of daily life. The rising healthcare costs stem in part from higher prices for hospital and other medical care, as well as the increased use of expensive prescription drugs — including GLP-1 weight loss medications — that are driving up spending for insurers and employers. The pressures are unique to each type of coverage. People who buy insurance through the Affordable Care Act marketplace, about 19 million adults, are set to face another year of steep premium increases after the enhanced federal subsidies expired last year. On Thursday, the White House promised $500 rebate checks to an estimated 1 million ACA enrollees, alleging they were wrongly overcharged. It’s unclear where the money for the rebates would come from or whether the distribution would require approval from Congress, but experts say it’s unlikely to provide significant relief. The $500 check “pales in comparison to the increased premiums that marketplace enrollees are facing due to the expiration of the enhanced subsidies,” said Miranda Yaver, an assistant professor of health policy and management at the University of Pittsburgh. Workers with job-based insurance may be asked to shoulder more of their employers’ rising health costs. And some Medicare beneficiaries could see changes to their prescription drug premiums after the Trump administration ended a temporary program that helped keep those premiums in check. Here’s what to expect. The Affordable Care Act People who buy health insurance through the ACA are on track for a second straight year of double-digit premium increases. Insurers who offer ACA plans are proposing a premium increase of about 15%, on average, for 2027, according to a KFF analysis of public filings from insurers across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. For 2026, insurers upped rates by an average of 20%. An individual earning $80,000 a year who doesn’t qualify for standard ACA subsidies could see the cost of their bronze plan — the cheapest plan — rise by roughly $80 a month, adding almost $1,000 to their annual tab. One of the biggest reasons insurers are hiking rates is that medical care is getting more expensive, Levitt said. Insurers have pointed to higher prices for hospital stays, doctor’s visits and prescription drugs, among other costs. Insurers generally “have felt pressure to add coverage of GLP-1 drugs for weight loss, but they’re also seeing big, big increases in costs for those drugs,” Levitt said. The ACA marketplace is also still adjusting to the expiration of the enhanced federal subsidies at the end of 2025. Those subsidies — first put in place during the pandemic — lowered monthly premiums for millions of people in the middle class. When they expired, people either paid significantly more for coverage in 2026 or downgraded their plans. The expired subsidies also led ACA enrollment to fall by about 3 million. Young adults — who are generally healthier and more likely to go without insurance when it becomes too expensive — accounted for a large portion of the enrollment decrease. That left insurers with a group of customers who, on average, need more medical care, Yaver said, which was also factored into insurers rates for 2027. Job-based health insurance Most Americans, about 165 million people, get health insurance through their jobs. Many of them may be feeling the price increases, too. Employers expect the cost of providing health benefits to each worker to rise 8.2%, on average, in 2027 — the largest increase since 2003, according to a survey of more than 1,800 employers by Marsh, a benefits consulting group. That doesn’t necessarily mean workers’ premiums will rise by 8.2%, said Dr. Kevin Schulman, a professor of medicine at the Stanford University School of Medicine who researches employer-based health insurance. Employers typically subsidize a large portion of workers’ health coverage. But when healthcare costs rise too sharply, Schulman said, employers have several ways of passing some of the increase along to employees. They can charge workers more for their monthly premiums, raise deductibles or make other changes to their benefits. Sometimes, they slow wage increases to offset the expense. “Because the costs are going up, the employers are trying to reduce the rate of growth, and the easiest way to reduce the rate of growth of healthcare costs is to push more of the costs onto the employee,” Schulman said. Many appear prepared to do just that. The Marsh survey found about two-thirds of large employers — those with 500 or more employees — said they expected to increase how much employees contribute toward their premiums in 2027. Others may shift costs in other ways, including waiving copays and deductibles for primary care visits while charging for other kinds of care, or keeping premiums the same while raising the deductible. For workers, that makes it important to look beyond the premium during open enrollment, Schulman said. A plan that costs less or about the same each paycheck may come with a higher deductible or require people to pay more when they seek care. Medicare Monthly premiums are handled somewhat differently for the roughly 70 million people enrolled in Medicare. People on Medicare generally have more than one premium to consider: typically, a premium for Part B, which covers doctor’s visits and other outpatient care; and, for 9 out of 10 enrollees, a separate premium for Part D, which covers prescription drugs. Prescription drug costs are where enrollees may see the biggest changes, according to Yaver, of the University of Pittsburgh. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services projected in July that the baseline monthly cost for Part D coverage will rise about 6% in 2027, from $38.99 to $41.33. What enrollees actually end up paying varies, depending on their income and their specific plan. The increase stems from the Trump administration withdrawing its support for a temporary federal program that helped offset premium increases for Part D plans. The program began in 2025 as Medicare’s prescription drug benefit underwent major changes under the Inflation Reduction Act. Without it, enrollees would have seen their monthly premiums nearly double, according to a report from the Government Accountability Office. The change will hurt seniors, Yaver said, noting that the program had reduced the average premium by 40% last year. People on Medicare are often retired and live on fixed incomes. “Though seniors don’t change their Part D plans often, this year may be an exception, potentially resulting in seniors opting into lower-quality plans, leaving them less protected,” she said. Enrollees will still have an annual out-of-pocket cap on prescription drugs. In 2027, the cap is $2,400.

articles.title: Natural compound in blueberries and grapes may unlock fat-burning process in muscle cells
articles.summary: A study published in Food Bioscience found pterostilbene from blueberries and grapes helped cultured muscle cells break down stored fat deposits.
articles.body: A natural compound found in blueberries and grapes may help muscle cells break down stored fat, new research suggests. In laboratory experiments conducted in Japan, researchers found that the compound, called pterostilbene, reduced fat accumulation in cultured mouse muscle cells. Pterostilbene is a naturally occurring antioxidant found in blueberries, grapes and other types of berries. While previous research linked it to metabolic benefits, little was known about how it could affect skeletal muscle. POPULAR SUMMER FRUIT HAS AN EDIBLE PART MOST PEOPLE THROW AWAY, USDA REVEALS The new findings, published Sept. 1 in the journal Food Bioscience, suggest that pterostilbene reduced abnormal fat buildup by encouraging cells to break down fat already stored in the cells. Fat buildup can result from high-fat diets, inactivity and aging, according to a news release. Too much fat inside muscle cells can interfere with how the body uses glucose and fatty acids and may contribute to insulin resistance. "Our findings establish a scientific framework for developing functional foods and nutritional supplements that target muscle fat metabolism," lead researcher Takakazu Mitani, an associate professor at Shinshu University, said in a statement. SEAWEED-BASED COATING COULD KEEP STRAWBERRIES FRESH FOR DAYS WITHOUT REFRIGERATION, STUDY FINDS The team screened several food-derived compounds in the cells and found that pterostilbene caused the strongest reduction in fat accumulation without disrupting muscle growth. It appeared to preserve a protein, PPAR-delta, that helps regulate how cells process fat, according to the study. The research also provides an "experimental framework" for identifying other natural compounds that protect PPAR-delta, Mitani added. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ While the findings provide a starting point for studying dietary approaches that could one day help address obesity, type 2 diabetes and age-related metabolic decline, future studies in humans and animals are needed to determine whether the effect translates beyond lab-grown cells. Using a cell model "strips away the complexity of human metabolism," Johannah Katz, a registered dietitian from Florida, told Fox News Digital. "In people, pterostilbene has to be digested, absorbed, metabolized, circulated and actually reach muscle tissue at an effective dose," she said. "We also can't assume mouse muscle cells will respond exactly like human muscle." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS While the study identified a potential mechanism that may help explain reduced fat accumulation in cells, that is different from showing that eating blueberries or taking pterostilbene supplements directly leads to fat loss, Katz added. "Blueberries and grapes are nutritious foods for many reasons, but this study alone doesn't show that eating more of them will reduce fat buildup in human muscle," she said. articles.title: Political fights can rip couples apart — therapist shares 3 ways to save a relationship
articles.summary: A marriage therapist reveals three strategies for couples navigating the political divide, from setting boundaries to finding compromise.
articles.body: More than one-third of Americans report having ended a relationship over political differences, according to recent research – and experts say those divisions may also be straining some marriages. Some high-profile couples, including Democratic strategist James Carville and his wife, Republican political consultant Mary Matalin, have remained together despite their differing views – but experts say navigating those differences isn't always easy. Anna Elton, Ph.D., a licensed marriage and family therapist and clinical sexologist in Massachusetts, said she has counseled couples on different sides of the political aisle. 'QUIET QUITTING' COULD SILENTLY DESTROY YOUR MARRIAGE – 4 WAYS TO BRING THE SPARK BACK "A lot of couples come in and they want to work on communication, and politics can come up in our sessions," Elton, author of "The Formula of Desire," told Fox News Digital. "I work with a number of couples who are in this place where they have a family, they have kids, but they can't talk about politics." For many singles, Elton said, political compatibility is now something they consider early in the dating process. WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY – PLUS THE 'RED FLAG' TO AVOID She referenced a recent study that found younger adults tend to make assumptions about religion, gender roles, empathy and other characteristics based on political affiliation. "So, before you get to know the person, you’ve already created this assumption of who this person is." "I've definitely been hearing from my younger clients who are saying, ‘I want to know which political party this person belongs to, and then I'll see if I want to even be going on a date and wasting my time with this person.’" COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS For couples who have been married for decades, today's political divisions may present challenges that didn't exist when their relationships began, Elton noted. The expert offered the following three tips for navigating politically charged conversations with a partner in a healthy way. No. 1: Set boundaries ahead of time Come up with rules for the conversation and set the tone before it starts, Elton suggested, noting that the first three minutes of a discussion typically predict the outcome. Conversations that begin with a harsh tone or accusatory language are unlikely to be productive, she said. "So, before you talk, say, ‘OK, these are our boundaries for this conversation.’" Those boundaries can also extend to media habits, Elton said, including limiting how much political content couples consume, especially on social media. "You read certain things and then all of a sudden, you keep scrolling on your social media and you see similar content coming up over and over and over again," Elton said. "And at this point, it creates an illusionary effect." HOW OFTEN ARE MARRIED PEOPLE HAVING SEX? WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT THE INTIMACY STANDARD IN AMERICA Hearing the same information repeatedly may lead people to gradually accept it as true, according to Elton. "Now think about two people who are in their echo chambers, and they're exposed to certain information that is contradicting each other." As a general rule, Elton said couples should be mindful not to spend more time on their phones than they do engaging with each other. Excessive screen time can reduce face-to-face connection, leaving less room for eye contact, conversation and other shared experiences. Also, when someone is constantly consuming political content, it can become the primary topic they want to discuss, creating tension when partners hold different views, she cautioned. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP To help reduce conflict, Elton recommended limiting when political news or posts are consumed. She also suggested setting aside one phone-free date night each week to encourage face-to-face connection. No. 2: Agree to disagree While couples with differing political views are unlikely to agree on every issue, "agreeing to disagree" can help prevent hostility. "We can still love each other," Elton said. "It's not going to affect our relationship." "As soon as it gets to the point of seeing your partner through the lens of ‘if you believe this, this is who you are, and I can’t believe that I'm still in a relationship with you,’ that becomes a problem." Elton urged couples not to take political disagreements personally and instead approach them with curiosity. She also recommended looking at the same information together, allowing each partner to ask questions and draw their own conclusions rather than jumping into a heated debate. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The therapist also encouraged couples to focus on areas of common ground rather than viewing disagreements in black-and-white terms. After a disagreement or failure to compromise, it’s important to always reconnect with your partner, she emphasized. Sharing reassuring words like "I love you" and "You matter to me more than anything else" can be helpful, she said. "I feel like you always need to say, ‘Hey, I hear what you're saying, but I'm not agreeing, and that's OK.’" 3. Consider the wider impact When politics come into play in a relationship, it can have an impact on more than just the couple. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Elton encouraged partners to consider how sharing certain opinions can impact other loved ones, especially if one person confides in a family member or friend about the other's views. "You can create this triangulation where you're connecting with someone against your partner, and you don't want that," she warned. "Talk to your therapist, vent to your therapist… because if you start venting to your family and friends, then they start forming certain opinions about your partner, and it can affect how they talk to them, how they interact with them." Before making any drastic decisions, such as ending a relationship over political discord, Elton suggested slowing down and returning to a more grounded state. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "We hear certain things and we fill in the gaps," she said. "When we hear someone's political affiliation, we often make assumptions about who they are without really hearing them out." Rather than making assumptions based on the media or podcasts a partner consumes, for example, Elton encouraged couples to ask questions, stay curious and remain open-minded.
